summary: No, the flake did not change in any way these spectra can resolve. Between day 1 and day 2 every MoS2 and Si line moved up by about +2.5 cm-1, but that shift is spectrometer calibration, not doping or strain. After correcting with the Si line, E2g and A1g positions agree to about 0.02 cm-1, the E2g-A1g separation is unchanged within error, and the peak intensities and widths are the same within error. The only real change is a flat background offset of about 137 counts on day 2, which does not scale with the Raman peaks and is not from the sample's Raman signal. The E2g-A1g separation of about 21.5 cm-1 is closest to the 2-layer value in Lee et al. (2010), but the laser wavelength behind that comparison is unverified, so treat the layer count as provisional.

observations.finding: All three lines (E2g, A1g, Si) shift by the same amount between days, so the shift is a rigid calibration offset.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fits, windows and line shapes varied (6 settings x 2 shapes): day2-day1 E2g +2.507, A1g +2.439, Si +2.492 cm-1; setting-to-setting spread <=0.006 cm-1. Si line 519.976 +/- 0.015 (d1) vs 522.469 +/- 0.028 (d2). E2g 383.325 +/- 0.013 vs 385.833 +/- 0.019; A1g 404.915 +/- 0.065 vs 407.349 +/- 0.10.

observations.finding: After referencing to the Si line, E2g and A1g are identical on both days, so neither doping nor strain is detected.
observations.evidence: Using Si = 520.7 cm-1 (commonly quoted room-temperature value, from memory): day 1 E2g 384.05, A1g 405.64; day 2 E2g 384.06, A1g 405.58 cm-1. Corrected shifts: E2g ~0.01 cm-1, A1g -0.06 cm-1, both within the ~0.1-0.3 cm-1 calibration uncertainty. An A1g-only shift would point to doping and an E2g shift with splitting change to strain; neither is seen.
observations.source: Chakraborty et al., PRB 85, 161403(R) (2012), arXiv:1206.1758 (A1g vs E2g doping/strain sensitivity, from memory, not checked against the figure)

observations.finding: E2g-A1g separation is unchanged between days (within error). The separation is independent of spectrometer offset because both peaks come from one spectrum.
The 21.5-21.6 cm-1 separation is closest to the 2-layer value in Lee et al. (2010). This is a read-off from their Fig. 2(b), so the layer count is approximate and provisional.
observations.evidence: Fig. 2(b) of Lee et al. (arXiv:1005.2509; ACS Nano 4, 2695): separation (right axis) about 19 cm-1 for 1L, about 21.5 for 2L, about 23.7 for 3L, about 24.5 for 4L, about 26 for bulk. Read-off error about +/-0.3 cm-1.
observations.source: Lee et al., ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010), arXiv:1005.2509, Fig. 2(b)

observations.finding: Peak intensities are unchanged between days, so there is no sign of a change in the sample's Raman response.
observations.evidence: Area ratios day2/day1: E2g 1.011, A1g 0.975, Si 0.985 (uncertainties about 0.02-0.05). A1g/E2g = 1.046 +/- 0.035 (d1) vs 1.009 +/- 0.052 (d2), difference not significant. E2g/Si = 0.561 vs 0.576, not significant.

observations.finding: The flat background rose by about 137 counts (1.38x) at 400 cm-1 with no change in peak areas, so it is additive and not a Raman change from the sample.
observations.evidence: Linear baseline at 400 cm-1: day 1 365.4 counts, slope -0.044 counts/cm-1; day 2 502.8 counts, slope +0.006. Peak areas scale-invariant (Si ratio unchanged), so the acquisition gain is the same; the offset is additive.

observations.finding: Peak widths are unchanged within error, so no defect or disorder change is detected.
observations.evidence: FWHM E2g 2.07 +/- 0.04 (d1) vs 2.14 +/- 0.06 (d2); A1g 6.35 +/- 0.22 vs 6.38 +/- 0.35; Si 3.54 vs 3.50 cm-1 (resolution unchanged). Residuals show no structure in either window.

observations.finding: The day-2 spectrum has a different sampling step (0.66 cm-1 vs 0.53 cm-1), which suggests a different spectrometer or grating setting between days.
observations.evidence: Median x step: day1 0.530 cm-1 (949 points), day2 0.660 cm-1 (756 points), both spanning 150.0-649.6 cm-1.

caveats: Calibration reference: the Si first-order line is taken as 520.7 cm-1 from memory (commonly quoted room-temperature value); no source was checked in this session. Using 520.5 cm-1 changes only the absolute values, not the day-to-day comparison.

Lee et al. Fig. 2(b) values are read off the figure (about +/-0.3 cm-1). The laser wavelength used by Lee et al. was not confirmed from the parsed captions, so their separation-vs-layer mapping may not apply exactly at 514.5 nm.

The separation-to-layer mapping depends on substrate, strain and laser; on a SiO2/Si flake it is a consistency check, not a layer measurement. AFM or optical contrast is needed to confirm the layer count.
The A1g width (about 6.4 cm-1) is large compared with E2g (about 2.1 cm-1); it is consistent between days, but whether that reflects instrument, a fit compromise or the sample is not established.
The Chakraborty et al. reference (A1g softens with electron doping, E2g insensitive) is from memory and was not checked against its figure; the doping and strain conclusions rest on it.

Day-to-day calibration differences of about 2.5 cm-1 are much larger than a typical strain or doping shift, so any real effect of 0.1 cm-1 or below cannot be separated from calibration noise with these two spectra.

The skill's reference notes and scripts live outside the working folder, which I was told not to read; the analysis was done with my own fit code (analysis/fit_peaks.py, analysis/robust.py, analysis/intensities.py), so the skill's QC, Si-calibration and relation checks were not applied.
questions_for_user: Was the spectrometer recalibrated or the grating/centre wavelength changed between the two days? The sampling step changed from 0.53 to 0.66 cm-1, and the Si line moved by +2.5 cm-1, which both point to a settings change.
Was there a Si reference (or a Ne/Hg lamp line) measured on each day? That would settle the calibration offset directly rather than inferring it from the Si line in the same spectrum.

What changed in the background (about +137 counts, flat)? Possible causes are a dark-offset or background-subtraction setting, stray light or room light, or surface fluorescence. Were integration times and the number of accumulations the same?
What laser power and objective were used on each day? Heating would shift lines down, not up, so power does not explain a +2.5 cm-1 shift, but a power change can still matter for other reasons.
Is the flake layer number known independently (AFM, optical contrast)? Only then can the 2-layer reading from the 21.5 cm-1 separation be checked.
Was the excitation 514.5 nm in both sessions, and was the polarization geometry the same? Both affect relative intensities and the A1g/E2g ratio.
citations: [arXiv:1005.2509 / ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010), Fig. 2(b)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.2509): E2g-A1g separation vs layer number, read off the figure

[arXiv:1206.1758 / PRB 85, 161403(R) (2012)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.1758): symmetry-dependent phonon renormalization in MoS2 (A1g vs E2g doping sensitivity); cited from memory, not checked against its figure
limits: What the data cannot tell: whether adsorbates doped or strained the flake at a level below about 0.1-0.3 cm-1 of phonon shift. The spectra also cannot give an absolute layer count, defect density or doping level without an external calibration relation.
Relations not applied: no quantitative doping or strain relation was used, because none was checked against a source in this session and the shift is within calibration.

Rejected hypotheses: (1) adsorbate doping (would shift A1g alone; no differential shift); (2) strain (would shift E2g and change the splitting; neither changed); (3) laser heating (would soften and shift Si down, not up); (4) fluorescence or PL as the cause of the peak shifts (the background change is additive, not tied to the peaks).
The skill's own reference notes and scripts were not used because they lie outside the working folder.
